sentences.text: The name Draconichthys elegans translates to "elegant dragon fish".
Its jaw plates are unusually large and bear long, prong-like structures.
Aside from these unique features, the skull anatomy resembles that of other selenosteids such as Enseosteus and Rhinosteus.
The only known specimen is a skull measuring exactly 112 millimetres in length.
Researchers suggest the animal used its pronged plates to stop prey from escaping.
The genus Draconichthys was named by Rücklin in 2011.
Fossils were found in the Anti-Atlas Mountains of modern-day Morocco.
Draconichthys belongs to the class Placodermi.
The genus is classified within the family Selenosteidae.
The only known species in the genus is Draconichthys elegans.
Fossils of Draconichthys date to the Late Frasnian stage.
The animal lived between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago.
Its habitat was a shallow sea dimmed by algae during the Late Devonian.
